requirements.summary: The installed rule targets the exact path and parses as a one-day policy. The native persistent daily logrotate timer was enabled and active both before and after restart.
The effective rule specifies rotate 7 and compression; a forced rotation reported rotateCount 7 and produced a gzip archive that passed integrity checks and persisted across restart.

requirements.requirement: Allow a writer to continue writing after rotation.
requirements.summary: A bounded writer held the same log inode before and after copy-truncate rotation, remained alive, and completed normally through sequence 30 after rotation.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use compatible software.
requirements.summary: The node remained on RHEL 10.0 with kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0. The existing packaged logrotate 3.22.0 was used and verified, with package health remaining clean.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The mandatory node-restart protocol is also complete: healthy pre-restart state, acknowledged restart scheduling, connection disruption, changed boot identity, and recovered configuration, archive data, scheduler, security services, and system health were directly observed. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently corroborate the restart.
limitations: A natural wall-clock daily run and seven successive generations were not observed; cadence and retention are established by the parsed effective configuration, active persistent timer, and one successful forced rotation.
No real inventory application process was present during discovery, so write continuity was demonstrated with a synthetic writer holding an open descriptor to the exact production log path.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Creating and installing the candidate rule was necessary configuration work (cmd-eac9b3a1108544fb, cmd-0934f219e85b43e8). The temporary writer and forced rotation were bounded behavioral evidence (cmd-ead32bf2db794e39, cmd-b3fbc79a8c434c1b); synthetic content and temporary files were removed while preserving the original data in the legitimate rotation archive (cmd-91cf4f1106cf4917). The reboot was required by the provider-wide protocol (cmd-6903e5df0242435f). Final observations show no test residue, failed units, unexpected listeners, package damage, or conflicting rules.
